name: PhysBench-Diag
description: A diagnostic partition over PhysBench v2 with a deterministic 5-subtype quantitative/qualitative whitelist (size, mass, number, distance, temperature). Released alongside per-model probing JSONs, permutation tests, predictor LOO output, and sensitivity-analysis outputs to enable systematic study of where vision-language model architectures lose quantitative-physics decodability.
citation: @inproceedings{anonymous2026qlens, title={Q-LENS: A Pre-Registered Probing Stress-Test of Vision-Language Quantitative-Physics Reasoning}, author={Anonymous}, booktitle={NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track}, year={2026}, url={https://anonymous.4open.science/r/qlens-/}}
rai:dataCollection: Inherited deterministically from PhysBench v2 (Chow et al., 2024). No new data collection by this submission.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Quant/qual annotations are deterministic functions of PhysBench v2 sub_type labels via src/optim/physbench_split.py:classify_quantitative(). No human annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement: N/A (deterministic). Validation: see PRE_REGISTRATION.md and the paper's Methods section.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PhysBench v2 items are partitioned using PhysBench's val (200 items) and test (9802 items) splits. Under the locked 5-subtype quantitative whitelist, val yields 55 quantitative + 145 qualitative items; test yields 999 quantitative + 8803 qualitative items. Per-model probing applies bnb-NF4 4-bit quantization (one model, IBM Granite-Vision-3.2-2B, in bf16 due to a documented dtype-mismatch issue), with forward hooks at four matched architectural sites (post-encoder, post-projector, decoder layer 8, decoder layer 16).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Hosted via the anonymous mirror at anonymous.4open.science during double-blind review. Post-acceptance the de-anonymized GitHub repository will host the canonical version. Errata via repository ERRATA.md.
rai:dataUseCases: Layer-wise probing of vision-language models on physics-reasoning tasks
Cross-VLM comparison stratified by quantitative vs qualitative physics tasks
Stress-testing compression-bottleneck hypotheses with locked kill-gates
Sensitivity analysis of probing definitions and partition choices
Reproduction and audit of pre-registered VLM evaluation studies
rai:dataLimitations: n=200 validation items is small for some statistical tests; the full n=9802 test split is also released for higher-power follow-ups.
14 of 200 validation items have unresolvable media paths in our local PhysBench mirror; flagged as no_media in probing JSONs.

Quant/qual partition is derived from PhysBench sub_type taxonomy under a 5-subtype whitelist; if PhysBench updates the taxonomy or a different whitelist is preferred, the partition must be re-derived. We document a sensitivity analysis on the whitelist choice in scripts/subtype_sensitivity.py.
Probing-feature caches are model-specific; new VLMs require new probing runs.

H3 hit-rate values for the 4 baseline models were derived under a different operational definition than the 6 active-set models; we document and analyze this asymmetry in scripts/h3_sensitivity_unified.py.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: enables more targeted improvement of VLMs on quantitative-physics tasks and provides a worked example of pre-registration plus sensitivity analysis as a discipline for VLM evaluation methodology. Negative: probing tools could theoretically be repurposed for adversarial analysis; we release only standard linear probes that do not enable novel attack capabilities beyond existing probing literature.
rai:dataBiases: Inherited from PhysBench v2; please refer to that benchmark's original analysis. Our partition does not introduce new biases beyond the choice of which sub_types are designated quantitative.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. PhysBench items are public physics-reasoning prompts.

distribution.name: h3_sensitivity_unified.json
distribution.description: Re-computation of H3 hit-rate for all 10 panel models under a unified above-chance criterion. Demonstrates the mechanism stratification falsification.

distribution.name: subtype_sensitivity.json
distribution.description: Sensitivity of pre-registered kill-gate to partition whitelist expansion (5-subtype vs. 8-subtype).

distribution.name: power_analysis.json
distribution.description: Spearman-rho minimum detectable effect at panel sizes 10-50 (alpha=0.05, power=0.80).

distribution.name: probing_results_n10
distribution.description: Per-model probing JSONs (10 models x {answer, task_type, sub_type} targets x {enc_out, post_proj, llm_8, llm_16} sites x {all, quantitative, qualitative} slices), plus 6 permutation_check JSONs. Released as individual files under results/week1_turing/ in the repository.
